Cagey

KAY-jee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cagey is wary, cautious, and tight-lipped; evasive when questioned.

The art dealer stayed cagey about where the painting had actually come from, changing the subject every time a buyer asked.

Worked Example

When a reporter asked point-blank whether the actor was leaving the franchise, he just smiled, said 'we'll see,' and quickly asked about the snacks on set instead.

Dodging a direct question with a vague non-answer and a quick subject change is exactly the wary, tight-lipped evasiveness cagey describes.

How Cagey Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

evasive

evasive: avoiding giving a direct answer

Antonyms

candid

candid: open and honest in expression

forthcoming

forthcoming: willing to give information freely

How Strong Is It? — guarded → cagey → evasive

guarded vs. cagey

guarded vs. cagey: Guarded is weaker than cagey: a guarded interviewee just holds back a little at first, while a cagey one stays warily tight-lipped, dodging even friendly follow-up questions.

evasive vs. cagey

evasive vs. cagey: Evasive is stronger than cagey: a cagey spokesperson answers carefully and gives little away, but an evasive one goes further, refusing to say anything about the merger at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Cagey is American slang first recorded in the 1890s, and its true origin is genuinely unknown. One guess connects it to cage -- an animal that once escaped a cage stays forever warier of being trapped again -- but the link has never been proven.

Word Choice

Cagey implies someone is deliberately withholding information, often suggesting they have something to hide -- contrast it with taciturn, which is just a quiet personality with no particular secret.
